system.summary: Simple substitution with invented signs (one per letter, O with two forms), words spaced, six null signs and five name/place signs (Lasry key).
system.notes: Name signs N1-N4 occur here (13 tokens); identifications withheld.

prior_solution.where: Lasry key table (05/11/2023) and an edited text of f.101r (as 'fr.3092 f.100') on Tomokiyo's cryptiana GL.htm; no text of ff.103-104 or f.107 anywhere found

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code and posed the problem with /goal (catalogue card 182, DECODE R3699-R3701). No target-specific intervention recorded.

solution.what: Repo grep and Tomokiyo's GL.htm list fr. 3092 ff. 101, 103, 107 in Lasry's fr. 3029 cipher; GL.htm prints Lasry's decipherment of 'f.100' (edited by Tomokiyo).
DECODE record pages R3699-R3701 fetched with the session cookie; 11 images downloaded (full-resolution leaves P2/P3/P5, openings as .jpeg).
Lasry's table applied to f.101r line 1: text matches Tomokiyo's; key applies unchanged.

f.101r (26 lines) transcribed by eye from overlapping band crops, each sign as its key letter; ff.103r-104r (65 lines) and f.107r-v (40 lines) given to two transcription subagents with a written brief.
f.101r compared with Tomokiyo's edited text: agrees. Sample lines of ff.103-107 checked sign for sign against the images.
lang.lm.best_language on the 4,521 letter signs: fr-1600-letters first (-1.93 vs fr-modern -2.12).
BnF inventory of fr. 3092 (cc49555w) fetched: nos. 43/44/46 'Mémoire chiffré'.
All three read (content, attribution and dating withheld).

outcome.method_basis: Lasry's key table for the fr. 3029 cipher, listed for fr. 3092 ff. 101, 103, 107 on Tomokiyo's cryptiana GL.htm, was applied unchanged; f.101r agrees with Lasry's decipherment edited on GL.htm, ff. 103-104 and 107 were transcribed and read here.
outcome.notes: All 131 cipher lines read with Lasry's key unchanged; 13 name-sign tokens have no key value. Withheld 22 Sept 2026 at George Lasry's request: he and a historian have deciphered and analysed these letters for their own publication. Readings, transcriptions and content are kept outside the public repository; counts and method fields stand as measured.
